A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same RHI research, despite the changed title and substantial revision. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices are readable, and retained material can be matched reliably.

before.justification: v2 Section 6 reports original Garnet G(20,15) simulations measuring RHI convergence under contamination, ℓ∞, and ℓ2 uncertainty.

after.justification: v3 Appendix A.2 retains the Garnet simulations, while Appendix A.1 adds original estimator-bias comparisons under KL and χ² uncertainty.

M1.justification: v3 retains the Halpern and recursive-difference backbone but introduces a K-order weighted multilevel estimator, KL dual-grid maximization, and χ² dual optimization. Algorithm 1 adds anchored bias functions and oracle-dependent sampling budgets. The earlier contamination/ℓp constructions remain in Appendix G.

E1.justification: v3 adds synthetic worst-case expectation estimation under KL and χ² uncertainty in Appendix A.1. This extends the evaluated uncertainty models and task requirements, but does not add full policy-learning benchmarks for those models. The original Garnet coverage is retained.

E2.justification: v3 Figure 1 newly evaluates standard MLMC against the proposed K-order estimator. The original RHI comparison with the RRVI-computed optimal robust reward remains unchanged in Appendix A.2.

E3.justification: Appendix A.1 introduces an estimator-level protocol measuring bias while sweeping K from 0 to 8 on randomly generated nominal distributions. The retained Garnet evaluation procedure is unchanged. Inner sample budgets and uncertainty radii for the new experiment are not specified.

E4.justification: v3 adds a sensitivity analysis testing how estimator order K affects bias relative to standard MLMC under KL and χ² uncertainty. v2 contains only the retained RHI convergence experiments, without this component-level analysis.

E5.justification: The retained Garnet experiment still specifies ten independent runs, means, and standard-deviation shading. The new estimator plots contain error bars, but Appendix A.1 defines neither those bars nor its run count. Whether they introduce a different statistical reporting practice is therefore unresolved.

E6.justification: v3 adds bias-versus-K results showing generally lower plotted bias for K-order MLMC than standard MLMC under both KL and χ² uncertainty. The three original Garnet convergence plots are identical to those in v2, and their convergence findings are retained.

T1.justification: Assumption 3.1 changes from communicating robust MDPs to global irreducibility, and the definition of H changes to cover all optimal policies and their worst-case kernels. v3 adds oracle assumptions, smoothness conditions, bias-cancellation and Lipschitz proofs, and KL/χ² complexity guarantees of order Õ(SAH²ε^−(2+o(1))). Appendix G retains the earlier contamination/ℓp rate.

C1.justification: The abstract and contributions shift from communicating-MDP guarantees and the tight ε^−2 rate for contamination/ℓp sets to a universal oracle framework and K-order MLMC for KL/χ² sets. The claimed weakest structural assumptions disappear; the headline comparison becomes asymptotic agreement with model-based complexity.

C2.justification: v3 substantially revises applicability and mechanism explanations. Remark 3.3 makes weakly communicating extensions conditional on a uniform solution-span bound, while Sections 5–7 explain the remaining complexity penalty through nonlinear-estimation bias. The conclusion adds specific limitations concerning generative-model access and extensions to online or offline learning.

D1.justification: Appendix F adds extensive oracle construction details: shared sample prefixes, explicit multilevel weights, KL grid spacing, numerical χ² maximization, and choices of K and N0. These substantially expand implementation guidance beyond v2's closed-form samplers. The existing Colab disclosure remains, while concrete settings for the new bias experiment remain incomplete.

R1.justification: v3 repositions RHI around model-free estimation and detailed comparisons with standard and truncated MLMC, especially in Sections 5.1.1 and 6.1. Table 1 explicitly distinguishes model-based and model-free methods. New references include Giles (2008), Vershynin (2018), and Roch and Wang (2025); many other reference changes are publication updates.

P1.justification: The abstract, contribution summary, method narrative, and conclusion are substantially rewritten. Experiments move from Section 6 to Appendix A, some related work moves to Appendix B, and the proof appendices are reorganized around the oracle framework. The title and author list also change.

P2.justification: v3 changes the main text and references from one-column to two-column formatting, restructures Table 1 with method-type labels and separate proposed-method rows, and adds a two-panel bias figure. The original three-panel convergence figure is relocated to Appendix A.2 and renumbered without changing its plotted content.

improvement.justification: Relative to v2's contamination/ℓp-focused treatment, v3 adds useful oracle specifications, broader constructions, explicit applicability limits, and direct bias comparisons. However, Lemma F.8 uses Equation (97)'s bound on absolute bias to bound expected absolute error after maximizing over dual parameters, without establishing that stronger bound. This unresolved step supports the new headline KL complexity guarantee, preventing a reliable net-quality judgment.
